settings.content: How the stone is held, and what that changes

settings.eyebrow: The Structure That Holds the Stone
settings.heading: There Is No Single Best Setting
settings.body:
The setting is the metal structure that holds each stone. It decides how much light reaches the stone, how protected it is, how the ring feels between the fingers, how much maintenance it will ask for, and how much room a jeweller has to work with if it ever needs resizing.

There is no single best setting. There is only the setting that suits the stone, the wearer and the way the ring will actually be used. A beautiful gemstone in the wrong setting is a risk; a more delicate stone in a thoughtful setting can be wonderful.

One distinction worth getting straight early: coverage is not a setting. Half eternity and full eternity describe how far the stones travel around the band. Any of the settings below can be used at any coverage.

settings.label: Solitaire
settings.heading: Solitaire, Plain Shoulders
settings.body: The timeless single-stone silhouette. Puts almost the entire budget into the stone and suits every hand. Browse solitaires.

settings.label: Solitaire
settings.heading: Solitaire, Diamond Shoulders
settings.body: A classic solitaire with brilliant shoulders. More sparkle across the finger without enlarging the centre stone.

settings.label: Halo
settings.heading: Halo, Plain Shoulders
settings.body: Haloed presence on a clean band. A halo makes a centre stone read noticeably larger for the money. Browse halos.

settings.label: Halo
settings.heading: Halo, Diamond Shoulders
settings.body: Halo and pavé shoulders together, for maximum sparkle. The brightest of the classic silhouettes.

settings.label: Halo
settings.heading: Hidden Halo
settings.body: A secret halo seen only from the side. Clean from above, a surprise in profile. Browse hidden halos.

settings.label: Multi-stone
settings.heading: Trilogy
settings.body: Three stones for past, present and future. Reads wider on the finger than a solitaire of the same total weight. Browse trilogy rings.

settings.label: Shoulders
settings.heading: Split Shoulders
settings.body: A divided band lifts and frames the stone, adding presence without adding carat weight.

settings.label: Multi-stone
settings.heading: Multistone Invisible
settings.body: Edge-to-edge stones with no visible metal between them. Modern and unusually bright. Browse invisible-set rings.

settings.label: Openwork
settings.heading: Oyster Deluxe
settings.body: An openwork basket cradles the stone, letting light in from beneath and lightening the whole design.

settings.label: Protective
settings.heading: Bezel
settings.body: A full metal rim, sleek and secure. The most protective setting there is, and the most snag-free.

settings.heading: Ten Settings, Compared
settings.intro: Illustrated at a consistent scale so the silhouettes can be judged honestly against each other.

settings.heading: Find Your Setting by Priority
settings.intro: If you only know one thing about what matters most, start from that and work back.

settings.cells: Claw or prong | Classic and open, light reaches the stone from all sides | Claws need inspection over time
Bezel / rubover | A protective metal rim framing each stone | Maximum protection, low-profile and snag-free
Half bezel | Partly surrounds the stone, leaving more of it visible | A balance of protection and light
Channel set | A continuous row held between metal walls | Highly secure and smooth, ideal for active daily wear
Flush / gypsy set | Stones sunk level into the band metal | Exceptionally practical, smooth surface for hands-on work
Pavé / micro-pavé | Tiny beads of metal holding closely set stones | High sparkle, periodic inspection, limited resizing
Shared claw / French pavé | Minimal metal between stones for maximum light | Maximum brightness, open sides need careful wear
Bar set | Stones separated by slim bars of metal | Geometric and art-deco in feel, good stone visibility
Scattered / starlight | Small stones placed at irregular intervals | Modern and characterful against matte or brushed metal

settings.heading: How Stones Are Actually Held
settings.intro: These are distinct settings, not interchangeable names. Shared claw, French pavé and grain-set pavé are often confused; they hold stones in genuinely different ways and they wear differently.
settings.headers: Setting | Visual profile | Practical and daily wear

settings.cells: Flush / gypsy | Low to medium | Very high | Low | High
Bezel / rubover | Medium | Very high | Low | Moderate
Channel | Medium | High | Low to medium | Moderate
Bar set | High | Moderate to high | Low to moderate | Moderate
Grain / pavé | High | Moderate | Medium to high | Limited
Shared claw / French pavé | Very high | Moderate | Higher | Limited
Full eternity | Very high | Depends on setting | Higher | Very low

settings.heading: Sparkle, Security and Upkeep
settings.intro: The things that matter after the first month. Nothing scores highest on everything, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling.
settings.headers: Setting | Sparkle | Security | Maintenance | Resizing flexibility
settings.note: Broad tendencies only. Stone size, metal thickness, craftsmanship and coverage all change the result.

settings.heading: Hidden halo
settings.body: Tiny diamonds tucked beneath the centre stone, visible only from the side. Clean from above, a private detail in profile.

settings.heading: Milgrain edging
settings.body: A row of tiny beaded metal dots along an edge. Characteristic of vintage and art-deco design, and it softens a hard line beautifully.

settings.heading: Gallery work and filigree
settings.body: Intricate metalwork beneath the head of the ring, seen only at close range. The part a jeweller judges another jeweller on.

settings.heading: Surprise diamonds
settings.body: Small accent stones set inside the band or under the basket, where only the wearer knows they are there.

settings.heading: Custom engraving
settings.body: A date, initials, a coordinate or a private phrase inside the band. Ask before the ring is finished, since some designs are harder to engrave afterwards.

settings.heading: Hidden Details That Elevate a Ring
settings.intro: These cost comparatively little and are what people notice years later.

settings.cells: Hands-on or active | Bezel, low-profile solitaire, flush-set band | Secure and snag-free above all
Desk-based or creative | Almost anything | Pavé, halo and three-stone all wear well
Hands in water often | Bezel or low-profile platinum | Avoid softer stones entirely
Vintage lovers | Cluster, milgrain, filigree, halo or hidden halo | Detail rewards close looking
Minimalists | Solitaire, east-west, bezel | A plain band with a stand-out stone

settings.heading: Setting by Lifestyle
settings.intro: A surgeon, a climber and a graphic designer all need different settings. A delicate vintage halo on a hands-on hand will catch, snag and eventually break.

settings.heading: Protective Setting Design
settings.body:
For emerald, aquamarine, tourmaline, opal, tanzanite and other more delicate stones, protection is not optional. Corners, edges and high settings are where damage begins.

A bezel, a lower profile, or a design that shields vulnerable corners can be the difference between a stone that lasts a lifetime and one that chips in its first year. Before choosing a delicate gemstone, ask us which settings will protect it properly. The stone and the design are one decision, not two.

settings.heading: Check What the Stone Can Take
settings.body: Hardness is not toughness, and the two are constantly confused. Our coloured stone guide covers the Mohs scale, which stones survive daily wear, and which need protecting.

settings.q: Which setting is the most secure?
settings.a: Bezel, also called rubover, where a rim of metal surrounds the whole stone. Flush or gypsy setting is close behind, with the stone sunk level into the band. Both are the sensible choice for hands-on work.

settings.q: Which setting gives the most sparkle?
settings.a: Shared claw and French pavé, because they use the least metal and let the most light in. The trade is exposure: open sides mean more careful wear and more frequent inspection.

settings.q: Can a pavé or eternity ring be resized?
settings.a: Sometimes, but the more stones travel around the band the less room there is to work. Half eternity resizes reasonably well, three-quarter is constrained, and full eternity is generally not conventionally resizable. Get the size right first time on those.

settings.q: What is the difference between pavé and French pavé?
settings.a: Grain or bead pavé holds stones with tiny metal beads, giving a continuous shimmer. French pavé cuts a V shape beneath each stone, reducing visible metal and letting more light in. They look similar in photographs and behave differently in wear.

settings.q: How often should a claw-set ring be checked?
settings.a: We recommend annually, and it is free for the life of the ring. Claws and pavé grains are the parts that loosen, and catching one early costs nothing while catching it late can mean a lost stone.

settings.q: Can I see the setting before it is made?
settings.a: Yes. Every bespoke ring goes through a 3D CAD render so you can see it from every angle, and we can produce a wax model if you would rather handle the design before we cast in precious metal. Edits are free.
